correctness.rationale: The poles 3±i√3 do not meet h(ω−1); the column-sum identity follows from r(0)=1. I independently inverted the denominator modulo X^n−1 over Q(h) and multiplied by the numerator for n=2,3,4; all nine factorizations agree. The two- and three-state coefficients are positive for h>0. In dimension four the only sign-changing coefficient is the first neighbor, with numerator −3hF(h) and a strictly positive denominator. Descartes and the sign at zero and infinity give exactly one positive root; F(6135/1000)=−642270159/1600000000 and F(6136/1000)=38072521/244140625 isolate it. All other entries remain positive at and beyond the crossing, and the h=0 map is the identity. For the asymptotic law solve (P−I)G=I−U and impose GU=0: the coefficient difference g_(j−1)−g_j=−1/n for j≥1 and the zero coefficient sum give g_j=(2j−n+1)/(2n), with the wraparound equation giving (n−1)/n. On the nonstationary Fourier modes r(hλ)=1+12/(hλ)+O(h^−2), while on the stationary mode r(0)=1 exactly. Reading off the first column gives the asserted coefficients and the strict eventual first-neighbor negativity for n≥4.
residual_risks: The asymptotic error is for each fixed n; no uniform estimate in n, stronger family claim, or claim about internal stages or finite precision is certified. The uploaded verifier was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: Probability mass can be conserved exactly while the update ceases to be a transition matrix. The exact root gives the safe substep range on the smallest failing cycle, e.g. a sufficient positivity condition for scaling and squaring, and the fixed-n asymptotics explain why convergence back to the identity does not imply eventual positivity. The four-cycle horizon is a substantive sharp boundary, not just a negative example at a chosen step.
residual_risks: No claim about efficiency of the resulting scaling condition in practice or positivity for arbitrary generators.
